Same paper's R and Teff: L = 2.48^2 x (6600/5772)^4 = 10.51 Lsun. Range given = the two. B alone: Mbol 5.00 -> 0.79 Lsun.

wikipedia.cross_check: Infobox R/Teff give 2.48^2 (6600/5772)^4 = 10.51 Lsun for A, consistent with Fuhrmann's Mbol (10.3). Infobox also shows component V 3.80 / 6.69.

nature: F2 IV subgiant (Fuhrmann: Teff 6600 K, log g 3.87, ~1.65 Msun)
notes: Fuhrmann's M_V,A = 2.26 for V_A = 3.80 implies a distance modulus of 1.54 (~20.3 pc, ~66.3 ly), matching the workbook's 66.35 ly. source: Waisberg, Klein & Katz 2023, RNAAS 7, 180 ('Hidden Companions to Intermediate-mass Stars. X. Solving for the Mass Ratio in the Spectroscopic Binary Zubenelgenubi = alpha2 Librae')
quote: We found that the primary is a M_Aa = 1.95 M_sun A2V star (T_Aa = 8200 K, R_Aa = 2.21 R_sun) ... the secondary is a M_Ab = 1.79 M_sun A7V star (T_Ab = 7930 K, R_Ab = 1.92 R_sun) ... The isochrone fit predicts magnitude differences Delta V_T = 0.44 and Delta B_T = 0.49.
derivation: L = R^2 (Teff/5772)^4 = 2.21^2 x (8200/5772)^4 = 4.884 x 4.073 = 19.9 Lsun, both inputs from Waisberg et al. 2023 (MIST isochrone fit to Tycho V_T, B_T, 2MASS K and the VLTI/GRAVITY K-band flux ratio 74.7%, at d = 23.24 pc from van Leeuwen 2007). Ab from the same paper: 1.92^2 (7930/5772)^4 = 13.1 Lsun.

wikipedia.cited_source: No luminosity in the infobox. alpha2 Lib A: M 1.95, R 2.21, Teff 8200 K; B (= Ab): M 1.79, R 1.92, Teff 7930 K, all cited to Waisberg, Klein & Katz 2023, RNAAS 7, 180 (2023RNAAS...7..180W)
wikipedia.cross_check: Same R/Teff as the derivation: 19.9 Lsun (Aa). No listed L to compare.

nature: A-type (A2V per Waisberg; MSC A3IV for the blend), the rapidly rotating member of the 70.3-d SB2
notes: Identification: Aa is the more massive star (1.95 Msun, matching the workbook's 1.97) and the brighter one in Waisberg's fit; Fuhrmann et al. 2014 (MNRAS 437, 2303) call it the rapidly rotating, 'almost invisible' A-type primary. Distance 23.24 pc = 75.8 ly, as in the workbook. Checks: combined V 2.75 (MSC), DM 1.831, BC_V -0.03 (Pecaut & Mamajek A3V-A4V) give 34.7 Lsun for Aa+Ab, against 19.9 + 13.1 = 33.0 from Waisberg; the Delta V_T = 0.44 split gives Aa 60% = 20.8 Lsun. The MSC's own split (Aa 3.15, Ab 4.03, dV 0.88; source not given, its note also quotes an occultation dB = 0.4) would give 69% = 24.0 Lsun; Zorec & Royer's combined 41.2 x 0.60 = 24.7. Plausible range ~20-25 Lsun; Waisberg's is the only direct component solution. Waisberg prints no uncertainties.

source: Tycho Double Star Catalogue (Fabricius et al. 2002, I/276) photometry of nu Sco D + Pecaut & Mamajek 2013 (intrinsic colours, BC_V) + workbook parallax
derivation: LOW CONFIDENCE. V(D) = V_T 7.23 (TDSC; V_T - V is a few hundredths for B9-A0). Reddening from neighbour C (2.4 arcsec): TDSC Bt-Vt(C) = 0.01 vs B8V intrinsic -0.107 -> E ~0.12; Gaia BP-RP(C) = 0.244 vs <= -0.12 intrinsic -> E(B-V) ~0.3; adopted E(B-V) = 0.20, A_V = 3.1 E(B-V) = 0.62 (range 0.37-0.93). DM = 5.756 (workbook 461.98 ly = 7.06 mas). M_V = 7.23 - 0.62 - 5.756 = 0.85. BC_V = -0.42 (B9V, the CD blend type 'B8V+B9VpSi' assigns B9 to the fainter star). M_bol = 0.43, L = 10^(0.4 (4.74 - 0.43)) = 53 Lsun. Low end: V 7.57 (MSC), A_V 0.37, BC -0.21 (A0V) -> 25 Lsun. High end: V 7.23, A_V 0.93, BC -0.42 -> 70 Lsun.

wikipedia.cited_source: No luminosity, radius or Teff for D. D: B9V (body text, uncited), V 7.23 (Fabricius et al. 2002, Tycho); distance 454.7 +/- 0.9 ly from D's own Gaia DR3 parallax. Body text says D is likely a spectroscopic binary and 'very little is known about Nu Scorpii Db'.

nature: late-B / early-A dwarf (B9V-B9.5V by catalogue type, B9III in the MSC), possibly the Si-peculiar member of CD; itself an unresolved pair Da,Db
notes: What is known: D = nu2 Sco B = HD 145501B, 2.4 arcsec from C (HD 145501A). The MSC marks D as Da,Db with code 's,a' (suspected spectroscopic, from 1983A&AS...52..471, plus astrometric: Gaia DR3 RUWE 4.707, plx 7.173 +/- 0.140); no orbit, period or mass ratio exists. Db's 0.5 Msun in the workbook is an inferred placeholder; if Db is a low-mass star its light is negligible and L(D) ~ L(Da), but nothing excludes a more luminous Db. Gaia DR3 gives no astrophysical parameters for D; TIC v8.2's 19.8 Lsun / 7624 K uses blended colours (prior pass). Photometry is inconsistent at the 0.3-mag level: V_T 7.23 (TDSC), V 7.57 for D and 7.39 for Da (both in the MSC), Gaia G 7.520 with BP/RP excess 1.26 (C's 1.21) - the 2.4 arcsec pair contaminates BP/RP. D's Bt-Vt (0.31) and BP-RP (0.39) are redder than C's (0.01, 0.24) by ~0.15, consistent with D being cooler than C under common reddening. Combined-light consistency: Zorec & Royer give HD 145501 (C+D) logL 1.881 (76 Lsun); Kochukhov & Bagnulo 2006 give logL 2.31 +/- 0.13 (204) at 133 pc; Gaia FLAME for C alone is 154.7. These disagree among themselves by a factor ~2, so no subtraction is meaningful. The MSC's 1.96 Msun (from absolute magnitude) corresponds to ~A2V, ~24 Lsun in Pecaut & Mamajek, i.e. at the low end, probably without an extinction correction. Distance: 7.06 mas (workbook, A's parallax) vs D's 7.17 mas: factor 0.97. Use only with an orange border; 'none' is defensible if a component-resolved Teff is required.
